extracted.intended_audience: health care providers, health insurance issuers, legal counsel, state regulators, and OCR/compliance officers
extracted.subtask_description: Interpretive guidance and final-rule definitions for applying section 1557 nondiscrimination obligations to health programs and activities, including scope of coverage, federal financial assistance, reasonable accommodations (auxiliary aids/companions), preemption questions, and research exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Private right of action under section 1557
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1557 authorizes a private right of action under any of the bases for discrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR declines to adopt regulatory text addressing the appropriate standards for private litigants and leaves standards for private enforcement to the Federal judiciary; OCR's own administrative enforcement procedures are addressed in §§ 92.303 and 92.304.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interaction with State and local laws / preemption
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal laws preempt conflicting State laws; title I of the ACA contains a preemption provision (42 U.S.C. 18041(d)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR will consider specific facts when determining whether an action that conflicts with section 1557 has a legitimate nondiscriminatory reason, and is adding § 92.3(d): “Nothing in this part shall be construed to supersede State or local laws that provide additional protections against discrimination on any basis described in § 92.1.” OCR declines to add regulatory text asserting blanket preemption language, noting general constitutional and statutory preemption principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: No interpretation or enforcement of EMTALA by this rule
rubrics_metrics.description: This rule concerns section 1557 and does not interpret or enforce the Emergency Medical Treatment and Labor Act (EMTALA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR does not enforce EMTALA, and EMTALA does not expand or limit the civil rights protections found in section 1557; commenters' requests to clarify EMTALA protections (e.g., pregnancy termination) are outside the scope of this rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Religious freedom and conscience protections exemption (§ 92.3(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Insofar as application of any requirement under the part would violate applicable Federal protections for religious freedom and conscience, such application shall not be required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example cited: 42 U.S.C. 18023 provides that nothing in section 1557 shall be construed to affect Federal laws regarding conscience protection, willingness/refusal to provide abortion, discrimination based on willingness/refusal to provide/pay/cover/refer for abortion, or participation in abortion training. OCR revised § 92.3(c) to reflect this.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of auxiliary aids and services
rubrics_metrics.description: The term 'auxiliary aids and services' is carried forward consistent with the 2016 Rule and with ADA regulations at 28 CFR 35.104 and 36.303(b), and provides examples of auxiliary aids and services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective communication requirements are addressed in § 92.202(a); § 92.4 is a definitional section (used by § 92.202(b)), so commenters' suggested broadenings were not adopted. A technical citation correction was made (title II 'qualified interpreter' citation corrected to 36.104).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'companion' and selection by individual
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘Companion’ means family member, friend, or associate of an individual seeking access to a service, program, or activity of a covered entity, who along with such individual, is an appropriate person with whom a covered entity should communicate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definition is consistent with 28 CFR 35.160(a)(2) (title II of the ADA) and prior proposed definitions; OCR agrees the individual with a disability should select their companion except where there are concerns of conflict of interest or suspected abuse. OCR declined to add provider-selection limitations because definition tracks existing ADA language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and scope of 'Federal financial assistance'
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal financial assistance includes grants, loans, credits, subsidies, contracts of insurance, and other types of assistance from the Federal Government, including Federal financial assistance that the Department plays a role in providing or administering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically includes advance payments of the premium tax credit and cost-sharing reductions and pass-through funding available to States via section 1332 waivers; typical tax benefits, exemptions, deductions, and most tax credits are generally not Federal financial assistance because they are not contractual; inclusion of specific types would risk unintentionally narrowing the definition. Health insurance issuers receiving payments through section 1332 reinsurance programs are subrecipients and subject to section 1557; pass-through funding to individual consumers would not be subject to section 1557.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'health program or activity' — covered operations
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘Health program or activity’ covers any project, enterprise, venture, or undertaking to provide or administer health-related services, health insurance coverage, or other health-related coverage, assistance to obtain such services/coverage, clinical/pharmaceutical/medical care, health research (including clinical research), or health education; and includes all operations of any entity principally engaged in those activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR adopts a broad interpretation applying section 1557 to health insurance and other health-related coverage; when an entity is 'principally engaged' in such activities, the whole entity's operations are covered unless a part can be demonstrated to be a truly separate legal entity. This restores a broader, program- or institution-wide application (in line with CRRA principles) rather than the narrower 2020 Rule approach. Examples and clarifications: patient billing and collection activities related to health programs are covered (including contractual arrangements); Medicaid, CHIP, and the Basic Health Program are included; whether a group health plan receives Department funds may affect coverage (further discussion in § 92.207).

rubrics_metrics.name: Application to health insurance issuers and scope objections
rubrics_metrics.description: Health insurance issuers are treated as health programs or activities when principally engaged in providing or administering health insurance or other health-related coverage, and thus all operations of such issuers can be covered when they are recipients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR rejects the 2020 Rule's limitation that health insurers are covered only to the extent specific plans receive Federal financial assistance; commenters' evidence that broader coverage would cause withdrawal from markets was unpersuasive in the absence of substantiating data. OCR notes entities may structure business units and, if they can demonstrate that part of operations are truly separate legal entities, those parts may not be subject to the rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fungibility of funds rationale and corporate-structure considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: OCR discussed fungibility of funds as a rationale for applying nondiscrimination obligations across an entity's operations but states reliance on that rationale is unnecessary to support the interpretation that a 'principally engaged' recipient's whole operations are covered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR acknowledges diverse corporate structures and permits entities to demonstrate that a part of their operations is a truly separate legal entity to avoid coverage; absent such demonstration, an entity principally engaged is liable for all operations. The rule's coverage is supported primarily by statutory text rather than fungibility alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of health and clinical research and permissible research criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Health research, including clinical research, is included within the definition of 'health program or activity.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inclusion of research does not alter the fundamental nature of how research is designed or conducted: criteria in research protocols that target or exclude populations may be appropriate where nondiscriminatory justifications related to subject health/safety, scientific study design, or research purpose establish appropriateness, consistent with the 2016 Rule preamble.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coverage of patient billing and collections as health program activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Billing and collection activities related to health programs and activities are covered by the rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR declines to add explicit new definitional language because existing rule language and precedent already prohibit covered entities, directly or through contractual arrangements, from discriminating in billing and collections related to health programs and activities.
